'''Ronald Arthur Doney''' is a British mathematician. He is Emeritus Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Manchester]] and a specialist in [[probability theory]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Academic and research staff (A-Z) - Department of Mathematics |url=https://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/about/people/academic-and-research-staff/ |publisher=University of Manchester |access-date=2 August 2025}}</ref> 

Doney completed his PhD at [[Durham University]] in 1964 under the supervision of G. E. H. Reuter.<ref>{{cite thesis |title=Some problems on random walks |author=Ronald Arthur Doney |publisher=Durham University |year=1964 |url=https://etheses.dur.ac.uk/8893/1/8893_5824.PDF?UkUDh:CyT}}</ref> He worked briefly at the [[University of East Anglia]], before joining [[Imperial College London]] as a lecturer in 1965. In 1970, he moved to the [[University of Manchester]], where he spent the remainder of his academic career.<ref name="Doney">{{cite journal |title=A Lifetime of Excursions Through Random Walks and Lévy Processes |url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.10257 |journal=Progress in Probability |volume=78 |year=2021 |editor1-last=Chaumont |editor1-first=Loïc |editor2-last=Kyprianou |editor2-first=Andreas E. |pages=1–4 |access-date=1 August 2025}}</ref>

In the mid-1970s, Doney published a series of papers on the growth properties of general branching processes, and often collaborated with [[Nicholas Bingham]].<ref name="Doney" /> From 1977 onward, he returned primarily to the study of [[random walks]].<ref name="Doney" />

During the 1990s, he had a 'relatively intense' collaboration with French probabilist [[Jean Bertoin]]. This emerged from Bertoin noticing Doney’s 1991 paper on [[Lévy processes]] in the ''[[Journal of the London Mathematical Society]]''. They eventually co-authored seven papers on conditioned random walks, six of which appeared between 1994 and 1997.<ref name="Doney" />

==Selected publications==
* {{cite journal |last1=Bingham |first1=N.H. |last2=Doney |first2=R.A. |year=1974 |title=Asymptotic properties of supercritical branching processes I: The Galton–Watson process |journal=Advances in Applied Probability |volume=6 |issue=4 |pages=711–731 |doi=10.2307/1426188}}
* {{cite journal |last=Doney |first=R.A. |year=1991 |title=Hitting probabilities for spectrally positive Lévy processes |journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society |volume=44 |issue=3 |pages=566–576 |doi=10.1112/jlms/s2-44.3.566}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Bertoin |first1=J. |last2=Doney |first2=R.A. |year=1994 |title=On conditioning a random walk to stay nonnegative |journal=The Annals of Probability |doi=10.1214/aop/1176988497 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ron-Doney/publication/226629397_On_conditioning_random_walks_in_an_exponential_family_to_stay_nonnegative/links/02e7e517bacb817ab7000000/On-conditioning-random-walks-in-an-exponential-family-to-stay-nonnegative.pdf}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Bertoin |first1=J. |last2=Doney |first2=R.A. |year=1996 |title=Some asymptotic results for transient random walks |journal=Advances in Applied Probability |volume=28 |issue=1 |pages=207–226 |doi=10.2307/1427918}}
* {{cite journal |last=Doney |first=R.A. |year=2012 |title=Local behaviour of first passage probabilities |journal=Probability Theory and Related Fields |volume=152 |pages=559–588 |doi=10.1007/s00440-010-0330-7 |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00440-010-0330-7.pdf}}
